statement: The function returns a result r and: (1) len(r) = n-1; (2) for every d with 1 <= d <= n-1, r[d-1] is exactly the number of subsets S of {1,...,n} such that S is connected in G (for every u,v in S, all vertices on the unique path between u and v in G lie in S), |S| >= 2, and max{dist_G(u,v) : u,v in S, u != v} = d. Here dist_G(u,v) is the number of edges on the unique simple path between u and v in G, and each subset is counted once by its set of cities.
preconditions: P(n, edges): n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 15; edges is a slice with len(edges) = n-1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(edges), len(edges[i]) = 2 and 1 <= edges[i][0] <= n and 1 <= edges[i][1] <= n; let G be the undirected graph on vertex set {1,...,n} whose edges are the unordered pairs {edges[i][0], edges[i][1]} for 0 <= i < len(edges); G is a tree, i.e. it is connected and acyclic (equivalently, every two distinct vertices have a unique simple path in G).
